ruling_says: widen `loop-variable-fresh-per-iteration` to every binding made in a loop body

why: N5's closed list names only the loop variable as fresh per iteration; widening to every body binding follows from block scope but goes beyond the item's text.
law_fix: Block scope is a designed deviation: a binding made in a block body, loop bodies included per iteration, ends with the block; a later read reaching an outer binding is refused.

ruling_says: a comprehension's walrus over a binding of the SAME function — a local or a parameter — writes through as python does
law_says: A walrus inside a comprehension is the same shape: its binding is local to the comprehension, so where a visible outer name is read after it, the program is refused (owner ruling 2026-11-06).
why: N5 says a comprehension walrus binding is local to the comprehension and a later outer read is refused; R-MH (after N5) writes through instead and names the departure ('Rejected: (a) refuse as the sentence said (costs a working program that agrees with python)'), but N5's text was not updated.
law_fix: Add to N5: a comprehension walrus over a same-function local or parameter writes through, as python; over a module or enclosing binding read later it is refused.

ruling_says: keep the refusal, steer "write a nested def"; message only
law_says: A local is visible from its let / var (or first assignment) to the end of its block.
why: python3 runs a lambda-typed local that calls itself because the body runs after the binding; N5's 'visible from its let' does not say whether the binding's own initializer, or a lambda inside it, is in range.
law_fix: A local is not visible inside its own initializer, lambda bodies included; a recursive local is a nested def.

ruling_says: refuse `for`, `with` and `except` targets under `global x`
law_says: = (and every augmented, tuple, star and walrus store) assigns a binding of the same function. ... A bare store that would cross a function boundary is refused with the steer "let x = … for a new local, or global x / nonlocal x to write the outer binding".
why: N6 says every store under `global x` writes the module binding (python's rule) while N5 makes construct targets fresh block bindings; the laws collide on this shape and neither decides it.
law_fix: A for, with or except target naming a global- or nonlocal-declared name is refused, with a steer to assign inside the body.

law_fix: A for, with or except target naming a global- or nonlocal-declared name is refused, with a steer to assign inside the body.
